g10-geography-ug1-t1.overview: Overview of the World’s Major Landforms sits inside Landforms of Africa. Landforms of Africa are the focus of Unit 1 of Grade 10 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it reviews the three major landforms of the world, mountains, plains, and plateaus, and how internal and external processes shape them. Then it sets out Africa’s location, size, and boundaries across the Equator and the two tropics. Next, it maps the four major landform regions of the continent, from the Atlas Mountains to the Ethiopian Highlands. Also it compares deserts, the Sahel, the savanna, the rainforest, and the Great Rift Valley. Students will also learn how landforms of Africa apply to real-life situations, such as farming, settlement, and travel.
objectives: Describe the three major landforms of the world and how they form.
Explain how internal and external processes create landforms.
Locate the major landforms of Africa and their four regions.
Identify the Atlas Mountains, the Sahara, the Sahel, the savanna, and the rainforest.
Compare the Great Rift Valley, the highlands, and the southern platform.
g10-geography-ug1-t1.simple:
Overview of the World’s Major Landforms in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, mountains, plateaus, and plains as the three major landform types.
  • Minor landforms such as hills, valleys, gorges, and basins.
  • How tectonic movement and volcanic activity build highlands, while water and wind carve lowlands.
  • Also continents, oceans, and coastal features like islands, peninsulas, and isthmuses.
g10-geography-ug1-t1.detailed:
Overview of the World’s Major Landforms — the essentials. First, mountains, plateaus, and plains as the three major landform types. Minor landforms such as hills, valleys, gorges, and basins. How tectonic movement and volcanic activity build highlands, while water and wind carve lowlands. Also continents, oceans, and coastal features like islands, peninsulas, and isthmuses.

  • Describe the three major landforms of the world and how they form.
  • Explain how internal and external processes create landforms.
  • Locate the major landforms of Africa and their four regions.
  • Identify the Atlas Mountains, the Sahara, the Sahel, the savanna, and the rainforest.
  • Compare the Great Rift Valley, the highlands, and the southern platform.

Across the far northwest, the Atlas Mountains extend through Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia. Deserts and grasslands, including the Sahara, the Sahel, and the savanna, dominate the massif. Along the east, the Great Rift Valley, the African Great Lakes, and the Ethiopian and Eritrean Highlands. Finally, the mountains and deserts of southern Africa, including the Kalahari and the Namib.

  • Explain how internal and external processes create landforms.
  • Locate the major landforms of Africa and their four regions.
  • Identify the Atlas Mountains, the Sahara, the Sahel, the savanna, and the rainforest.
  • Compare the Great Rift Valley, the highlands, and the southern platform.
